rows.author: K005;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING GREEN LANES FOR STRATEGIC INVESTMENTS
rows.abstract:
Establishes a One-Stop Action Center for Strategic Investments to streamline and expedite the issuance of permits, licenses, certifications, or authorizations.
Characterizes Strategic Investments through the following:  significant capital or investment, consequential economic impact, positive impact on the environment, and notable contribution to the balance of payments, with complex technical processes and engineering designs, and improvement in infrastructure capabilities.
Includes, but shall not be limited to Highly Desirable Investment Projects recommended by the Fiscal Incentives Review Board; Foreign Direct Investments per implementation by the Foreign Investment Promotion and Marketing Plan; and Projects under the Strategic Investment Priority Plan (SIPP).
Related Topics:  Executive Order No.18; R.A. No. 9485, as amended by R.A. No. 11032 (Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018); R.A. No. 11534, R.A. No. 11234 (Energy Virtual One-Stop Shop Act); Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2023-05-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE FISCAL REGIME FOR THE MINING INDUSTRY
rows.abstract: Proposes provisions regarding the following:  royalty payments of 3% on gross output of large-scale metallic mining operations within mineral reservations, graduated rates on the profit margin of large-scale metallic mining operations outside mineral reservations, and 1/10 of 1% of gross output of small-scale metallic mining operations; margin-based windfall profits tax gained on all mining operations; registration of small-scale miners with the Mining Board and the Mines and Geosciences Bureau; ring-fencing which prevent the consolidation of income and expenses of all mining projects by the same taxpayer; thin capitalization - so that businesses will not depend on excessive debt funding; exemption of mining contractors from the confidentiality clause of the NIRC of 1997, as amended; institutionalizes the Phil. Extractive Industry Transparency Initiative (PH-EITI); and the creation of a Natural Resource Trust Fund from the revenues collected from the margin-based royalty.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08937

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A 30-YEAR NATIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE PROGRAM
rows.abstract:
Aims to establish a sustained vital infrastructure projects to be undertaken and implemented by concerned national government agencies and GOCCs in the field of  transport (roads, ports, airports, transport projects within the supply chain, infra provision, policies, environmental standards, etc., funds through asset management, different transport mode and healthy competition, “user-pays” principle, engineering enforcement and education, shift from private to public transport esp. on mass transport, inter-island shipping, inc. RORO, infrastructure in support of agriculture, tourism, trade and industry; energy (power generation, electricity costs, natural gas industry, renewable energy such as wind and solar, electricity transmission, services to unelectrified off-grid, island, remote, and last-mile communities; energy efficiency and conservation); water resources (fragmented management, master plans and multipurpose projects as irrigation, power, supply and flood control, investments in water supply, sewerage, and sanitation, flood control in major river basins and urban centers combining engineering intervention works with non-structural measures: land use management, watershed conservation, and flood info and warning systems), ICT (digital infra to complement the national broadband plan, address the gaps in connectivity, e-government for e-governance, system enhancement, climate-smart and resilient, ICT operators service obligations and performance standards, cost of broadband thru infra sharing policies, direct gov´t investment in network infra, broadband network and free wifi programs to be transitioned to private sector, permits for cellular towers, cable laying & network deployment, access to satellites, 5G or higher generation and technology social (Schools for the Future, modern health facilities, preventive care against diseases, social housing and resettlement, Solid Waste Management, prison infrastructure/jails,  and agri-fisheries modernization and food logistics.
	 	 
  
Proposes several general provisions regarding the following:  attainment of long-term development vision; ensures consonance with the National Physical Framework Plan and Land Use Plan, and Regional Development Plans; initial list of priority core national projects based on a) Phil. Dev´t Plan, 2017-2022 NEDA; b) Flagship Projects; and c) Programs and Studies of DPWH, DOTr, DOE, DICT, DepEd, DOH, BCDA, NIA, MWSS, among others; prioritizes projects based on effectiveness in meeting gov´t objectives; economic feasibility; social inclusion; environmental sustainability; security; public access; and technical readiness for implementation. . . ; private sector participation; asset preservation and maintenance; climate change adaptation, disaster resilience, and updated safety, health, and environmental standards against calamities and other hazards; infrastructure-related research and development; multi-sectoral, multi-modal and area-wide development; complete functional structures, and continuity in funding and implementing multi-year projects.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-05-22, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-05-24 and received by the Senate on 2023-05-24

“Section 53. 
Negotiated Procurement - Negotiated Procurement shall be allowed only in the following instances:  . . .
IN ALL CASES OF NEGOTIATED PROCUREMENT, ALL SUPPLIERS, CONTRACTORS, AND CONSULTANTS ARE MANDATED TO SUBMIT DOCUMENTS TO PROVE THEIR FINANCIAL CAPACITY.  THE PROCURING ENTITY SHALL ASCERTAIN THE FINANCIAL, TECHNICAL, AND LEGAL CAPACITY OF SUPPLIERS, CONTRACTORS, OR CONSULTANTS.”
